scope: Task 3 implemented service/model core only. Pipeline/UI integration, Task 2 extraction persistence, and full PostgreSQL concurrency verification remain separate work.

findings.title: Project changes silently disconnect inherited human revisions
findings.evidence: Ancestor lookup filters standard_code before checking source identity. A user corrects automatic LAB_WBC=62 to LAB_HGB=130 g/L. The next parser emits LAB_HGB=131 at the same page/polygon. The resolver returns AUTOMATIC 131 with no applied revision and no conflict, since the old automatic row still has LAB_WBC.
findings.consequence: A parser mapping change can silently replace an existing human correction, violating the explicit continuity requirement.
findings.requested_change: Match stable source identity independently of automatic project code, include effective corrected identities, and expose explicit unmatched/ambiguous revision conflicts instead of silently discarding them.

findings.title: A later parse clears an unresolved inherited conflict
findings.evidence: A automatic62/user6.2 -> B automatic63 -> user DEFER on B -> C automatic63. B effective revision_conflict is true, while C becomes false and still uses 6.2. The assignment recomputes only B automatic versus C and overwrites the true flag loaded from revision.after.
findings.consequence: An unresolved transcription/source conflict stops blocking downstream quality admission without any reconciliation.
findings.requested_change: Preserve unresolved ancestor conflicts across lineage; only clear a conflict through a recorded reconciliation of its actual source/value disagreements.

findings.title: Appending a status event loses the inherited value source
findings.evidence: After A user6.2 is inherited by B automatic63, DEFER on B keeps effective6.2 but switches original_observation_id from A to B, removes carried_source_evidence, and creates a revision linked only to B evidence. The snapshot excludes the originating observation/evidence and subsequent resolution no longer enters the inherited branch.
findings.consequence: The surviving human value is attributed to the newer automatic source rather than the evidence/revision that supplied it; later read paths cannot reliably return to its corresponding source.
findings.requested_change: Persist originating observation, revision, and evidence identity through snapshots or explicit lineage fields, distinguishing the action source from the source of each retained value.

findings.title: Any field correction clears every reparse conflict
findings.evidence: A automatic62/user6.2 -> B automatic63. CORRECT with raw_unit equal to its existing value removes revision_conflict while preserving effective6.2 and automatic63; the value/source disagreement was untouched.
findings.consequence: An unrelated or no-op field edit can silently remove the restriction for a still-conflicting value.
findings.requested_change: Track and reconcile the specific conflicting fields/sources, or require a separate explicit full-conflict reconciliation action; ordinary edits must preserve unrelated conflicts.

observations: Owner checks, explicitly assigned staff permission checks, revocation/expiry checks, active-version guards, document aggregate locking, and revision compare-and-swap are present. Static review did not establish a concrete unauthorized-access or PostgreSQL deadlock defect in these scoped service paths.

Reported tests cover simple reparse continuity, owner-versus-reviewer staleness, grant revocation, and OCR-score preservation, but omit project-code changes and multi-hop lineage with an intervening status action.

validate_observation defaults to default_dictionary even when revisions carry mapping_dictionary_version. Version-aware dictionary selection should be verified in the independently implemented publication/read integration; this review does not assert that integration is complete.
Comparator <3 against report range <5 returns unavailable. This is conservative and was not promoted to a defect.
